description: HYDRAFloods is SERVIR-Mekong's Python software for producing surface-water maps from multiple Earth-observation sensors. It combines image collections, filtering, terrain corrections and water-classification algorithms through Google Earth Engine. Users supply an area, dates, sensor collection and processing parameters; outputs are water masks and exported raster maps. Geographic coverage is configurable, with a documented Sentinel-1 example for Cambodia and the Mekong region. Public source and usage instructions are free under MIT. A limitation is that cloud services require separately configured accounts and permissions, and observed water extent depends on sensor conditions and algorithm thresholds. A water mask alone does not estimate flood depth or distinguish all permanent water. HYDRAFloods can prepare inundation observations to compare with flood-infrastructure simulations such as Delft3D FM (model-delft3d-fm). The README documents a complete mapping workflow and cites the software and water-detection method. No Earth Engine session, cloud export or imagery download was attempted.
